extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and registered patent agents interacting with IPOS (Singapore)
extracted.subtask_short: Singapore patent filing and renewal procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and eligibility requirements for ASPEC/PCT-ASPEC/ASPEC AIM pilots, Collaborative Search & Examination (CS&E), SG IP FAST acceleration, grant procedures (forms, title rules, excess claim fees), certificate issuance/regeneration, and patent renewal/expiry/restoration under IPOS. Focused on applicants and agents using IPOS systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT-ASPEC scope and acceptable PCT results
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT-ASPEC is an extension of ASPEC to include the use of PCT results established by an ASEAN IP Searching and Preliminary Examining Authority. PCT results acceptable under PCT-ASPEC include written opinion of the International Search Authority (ISA), written opinion of the International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA) or International Preliminary Examination Report (IPER) issued within the PCT framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the steps in Chapters 7.3.4 to 7.3.9 in addition to indicating PCT-ASPEC request on cover letter or ASPEC Request Form and emailing monitoring authority with requisite details (PCT application no.; desired 2nd AMS and application number in the 2nd AMS; Date of request; Applicant’s name).

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT-ASPEC request content and notification procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should: Indicate the request for PCT-ASPEC on the cover letter or on the ASPEC Request Form under remarks; and email the monitoring authority and PCT-ASPEC focal point with PCT application no., desired 2nd AMS and application number, date of request, and applicant’s name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email contact provided: PT_acceleration@ipos.gov.sg (also notify the PCT-ASPEC focal point). This procedural step is required in addition to the normal ASPEC steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT-ASPEC quota limit (pilot cap)
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT-ASPEC is a pilot programme with the number of eligible PCT-ASPEC requests capped at 100 per year starting from 27 Aug 2019 and ending on 26 Aug 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests beyond the cap are not eligible. Applicants should be aware of yearly limits when planning acceleration requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC AIM purpose and priority timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: ASPEC AIM prioritises Industry 4.0 patent applications. The AMS will issue first actions within 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of IPC codes relating to Industry 4.0 patent applications can be found on the IPOS website. The steps in Chapters 7.3.4 to 7.3.9 apply, plus indication of ASPEC AIM on cover letter/ASPEC Request Form and emailing monitoring authority with application details.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC AIM request content and notification procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should indicate the request for ASPEC AIM on the cover letter or on the ASPEC Request Form under remarks; and email the monitoring authority and ASPEC AIM focal point with: application no. from first IP Office; desired second IP Office and application no. in the Second IP Office; date of request; applicant’s name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same email monitoring contact (PT_acceleration@ipos.gov.sg). This is in addition to ASPEC procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC AIM quota limit (pilot cap)
rubrics_metrics.description: ASPEC AIM is a pilot programme with the number of eligible ASPEC AIM requests capped at 50 per year starting from 27 Aug 2019 and ending on 26 Aug 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure their requests fall within the annual cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent cooperation (re-registration) with Cambodia and Laos — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Under cooperation, patent owners/applicants in Singapore may re-register their Singapore patents at MISTI (Cambodia) or DIP (Laos), or submit an IPOS-issued search and examination report for grant in Cambodia or Laos, provided the Singapore application is related to the Cambodian or Laotian application (there is a priority linkage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure a priority linkage exists and follow IPOS website guidance for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-registration eligibility conditions — Cambodia
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions for re-registration in Cambodia: (a) The Singapore patent must be in force at the time of lodgement of registration request at the MISTI; (b) The Singapore patent must have a date of filing on or after 22 Jan 2003; (c) The Singapore patent must meet the Cambodian requirements for patentability, i.e., the patent relating to the Singapore patent must not be of a pharmaceutical nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must verify force status, filing date, and subject-matter eligibility before applying for re-registration in Cambodia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-registration eligibility conditions — Laos
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions for re-registration in Laos: (a) The Singapore patent must be in force at the time of lodgement of registration request at the DIP; (b) The Singapore patent must have a date of filing on or after 17 Jan 2002; (c) The Singapore patent must meet the Laotian requirements for patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check force status, filing date thresholds, and local patentability rules applicable to Laos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents required for re-registration in Cambodia or Laos
rubrics_metrics.description: The following documents are required for Re-registration in Cambodia or Laos: a. Official Request Form; b. Patent Application Fees; c. Certified copies of Singapore Certificate of Grant; d. Final specifications of Singapore patent; e. Copy of Abstract of Singapore patent; f. Certified Khmer/Laotian translations of abstract and final specifications of Singapore patent (within 6 months of submission for Cambodia); g. Power of Attorney, if an agent is appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure certified translations (where required) are recent (within 6 months for Cambodia) and procure certified copies of the Certificate of Grant and final specifications. Power of Attorney needed if using an agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of IPOS-issued Search & Examination reports to Cambodia/Laos
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applicants in Singapore with a related patent application in Cambodia or Laos can submit a written request to IPOS for IPOS to transmit a copy of the final search and examination report and the final specifications of the Singapore related patent application to the MISTI or DIP for the grant of the related patent application in Cambodia or Laos, respectively. Applicants can also request for the specifications of the related patent application in Cambodia or Laos to be amended accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit written request to IPOS; refer to IPOS website for more details on process and required documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative Search & Examination (CS&E) pilot scope and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: CS&E is a pilot programme with IP Viet Nam to provide enhanced prior art search and examination results based on combined expertise; complimentary during pilot from 1 Mar 2023 to 28 Feb 2025; CS&E report will be issued within 10 months from date of receipt of the Request for CS&E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CS&E is intended to speed the patent process for protection in both countries; note complimentary nature is only during pilot duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: CS&E caps and quota rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of CS&E requests will be capped at 20 requests per year for an initial duration of two years. There is also a further cap of two requests per month and a restriction of two requests per entity (individual or corporate) per month. Unutilised quota will be rolled over to the following month, subject to a maximum cap of four per month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan filings to respect annual and monthly caps; entity-level caps limit per-corporate/individual usage; rollover is limited to a max of four per month.

rubrics_metrics.name: CS&E eligibility conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for the CS&E programme, the following conditions have to be met: a. Application must be first filed in Singapore or Viet Nam, i.e., no priority claim and not a divisional application; b. The request for the grant of a patent, request for search and examination report and request for CS&E should be filed on the same day; c. Application should contain 20 or fewer claims, including 3 or fewer independent claims; d. Applicant must respond within 2 weeks from the date of receipt of Formalities Examination Adverse report (if issued); e. The request for CS&E is made within the cap limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All eligibility criteria are conjunctive—each must be satisfied. Pay attention to claim counts and required contemporaneous filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: SG IP FAST (patent acceleration) eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for patent acceleration under SG IP FAST, the following criteria have to be met: a. Application must be first filed in Singapore i.e., no priority claim; b. Patents Form 1, prescribed fee and complete patent specification is filed; c. Patents Form 11 and prescribed fee is filed on the same day as Patents Form 1; d. Request for acceleration under SG IP FAST indicated on Patents Form 11; e. Application must contain 20 or fewer claims; f. Applicant needs to respond within 2 weeks from the date of receipt of Formalities Examination Adverse report (if issued); f. Applicant needs to respond within 2 months from date of receipt of written opinion (if issued); g. Reason(s) for requesting acceleration and the technology field to which the invention relates has to be furnished on Patents Form 11; and h. The request is within the cap on the number of requests that is imposed for the programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note duplicate lettering in source (two 'f' entries). The respondent must meet each timing and filing requirement; indicate reasons and technology field on Form 11; the programme is capped—ensure quota availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: SG IP FAST related trademarks/designs acceleration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants with a patent application accelerated under SG IP FAST can request acceleration of related trademark and registered design applications within 12 months from the date on which the applicant is notified of the successful request for patent acceleration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to support coordinated IP portfolio management. Request must be within 12 months of successful patent acceleration notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Eligibility and timing to request grant
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications lodged on or after 14 Feb 2014, the Registrar will issue a Notice of Eligibility to proceed to grant if there are no unresolved objections in the search and examination, examination, supplementary examination or examination review report. The applicant may proceed to request issuance of certificate of patent within 2 months from the date of notification. Otherwise, the application will be abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing of Patents Form 14 within the 2-month window (or obtain extension) is essential to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for grant (Patents Form 14) and consolidated specification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To request for the grant of a patent, the applicant may file Patents Form 14 together with a clean copy of the consolidated specification including drawings (if any) incorporating any amendment or correction or missing part. For PCT national phase entry applications where the specification has been amended with the amendments annexed to the IPER and these amendments have NOT been incorporated in the specification of the application, the applicant is required to furnish a copy of the consolidated specification incorporating all amendments at the time of filing Patents Form 14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consolidated specification incorporates all amendments/corrections/missing parts at time of Form 14 filing. Late consolidated specs require extension of time as per later rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees at grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess claims fees would be charged if – (a) Number of claims at grant > number of claims at search and/or examination request (Patents Form 11/12); and (b) Number of claims at grant > 20 claims. If excess claims fees have been paid during the search and/or examination report request (Patents Form 11/12), there will be no excess claim fees at grant if there are no additional excess claims added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the manual illustrate how excess claims are calculated and fees applied. Planning claim counts across filings avoids unexpected excess fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of invention rules for Certificate of Grant
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of invention reflected on the Certificate of Grant depends on filing route: (a) For PCT national phase applications proceeding to grant, the Registry will rely on the title of invention which is published on the PCT Gazette if there are no amendments made; (b) For PCT national phase applications not originally filed in English, the Registry will rely on the title on the PCT Gazette unless the applicant requests to retain the translated title by indicating preference on Patents Form 14 or cover letter; (c) For national applications searched and examined by IPOS proceeding to grant, the title will follow that which has been approved or amended by the Patent Examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who wish to retain or change titles must clearly indicate preferences on the cover letter accompanying Patents Form 14 or file Patents Form 13 selecting the appropriate option related to Rule 47(6). Voluntary amendments to the title of invention are not possible except by the prescribed amendment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer pre-issuance checklist for Certificate of Grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the request is received, the Formalities officer will review the following requirements – a. Fee has been paid; b. Date of filing has been accorded; c. Preliminary examination has been cleared; d. National security clearance has been issued, if applicable; e. The application is not treated as abandoned, withdrawn, refused or granted; f. Representation details and/or address for service on this form correspond with that on record; g. Examination report has been established from request for Search and/or Examination Report (Patents Form 11/12), Supplementary Examination Report (Patents Form 12A), or Examination Review Report (Patents Form 12B/13); h. The Examination report does not contain unresolved objections on lack of unity; i. Notice of Eligibility has been issued; j. The form is filed within 2 months from the date of issuance of Notice of Eligibility or extension approved; k. A set of consolidated specification is filed if required and within time; l. Consolidated specification aligns with all amendments/corrections/missing parts on record; m. Title of invention on record is the same as the consolidated specification; n. Number of claims indicated on the form corresponds to the number of claims in consolidated specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any requirements are not met, the Formalities officer will invite the applicant to clarify or rectify within 2 months, with a reminder if necessary. Rectifications typically use Form CM4 (correction types), CM1/CM2 for representation changes, and eCommunications for clarification letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification procedure for errors before grant
rubrics_metrics.description: To rectify errors, the applicant may file Form CM4 and indicate the relevant rule in which the correction is sought (Rules 58 and/or 91). Options include: 'Correction of Form lodged' for errors on the form; 'Correction of Specification of a Patent or of an Application for a Patent' for errors on the consolidated specification; 'Correction of any other document relating to a Patent or an Application for a Patent' for errors on other documents. Overpayments due to additional number of claims indicated on the form will be refunded after filing Form CM4; underpayments will be calculated and paid with Form CM4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified CM4 correction types. For title discrepancies due to translations or examiner changes, the officer will clarify with the applicant; voluntary amendments to the title are restricted and have prescribed routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal and publication if objections unresolved
rubrics_metrics.description: If the objections cannot be overcome or there is no response from the applicant, the request will be refused and the applicant will be notified via letter. If the prescribed time period for putting the application in order has passed, the patent application status will be updated to 'Abandoned (EOT possible)'. The refusal will be published in the Patents Journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely responses to Formalities officer letters are essential to avoid refusal/abandonment and public publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance and formatting of Certificate of Grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Before issuing the Certificate of Grant the Formalities officer will ensure that: a. information reflected in the certificate of grant is correct and the presentation is neat (Font: Times New Roman, Font size: min 10); b. information such as title, applicant, inventor, priority details etc should be updated if necessary; c. if the certificate runs into more than one page, ensure that the details of the applicant is on the same page as the signature. With effect from 14 Feb 2014, the Registry uses an electronic format and a soft copy will be sent to the eCommunications inbox in IPOS Digital Hub. Certificates issued on/after 31 Jan 2010 will bear the Singapore National Coat of Arms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should download the granted patent specification from IPOS Digital Hub as the certificate will not be accompanied by the specification. Check eCommunications inbox for soft copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regeneration or revision of Certificate of Grant
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is an error in the certificate, the applicant may request for regeneration of certificate via eCommunications. The Formalities officer will assess the request and regenerate the certificate if there is an error on IPOS's part. If there are changes/corrections filed after the Certificate of Grant is issued, the applicant may file Form CM12 to request for a revised copy of Certificate of Grant (note on form to highlight request for revised Certificate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regenerated/revised certificates will be sent via eCommunications. Use the specified forms and clearly indicate purpose (regeneration vs revised copy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term and renewal start (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a patent is 20 years from the date of filing of the patent application (subject to patent term extension where applicable). The proprietor is required to renew the patent annually, starting from the fourth anniversary. The patent will lapse if the renewal fee is not paid within the prescribed period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners should track renewal dates and commercial value to decide maintenance. Patent term extension rules are in Chapter 9.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal form and reduced fees for Licence as of Right
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent may be renewed using Patents Form 15. If the patent has been endorsed with Licence as of Right (LOR), the patent can also be renewed with Patents Form 15, with renewal fees halved. Once a request to cancel the LOR is approved, the balance of the previously halved renewal fees will have to be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of LOR status and fee consequences of cancelling LOR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online renewal acknowledgement and success criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: For patent renewals done via IPOS Digital Hub, the Acknowledgement Advice generated at the end of the online transaction will be taken to be the Notification of Renewal for the renewing period. An online renewal transaction will be considered successful when the required fees are successfully deducted. If deduction is not successful, the user will be notified and the Acknowledgement Advice is void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm successful deduction and retain the Acknowledgement Advice as proof of renewal. Monitor bank/payment failures promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may renew and renewal timing windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone can renew a patent. It is not necessary for the authorised agent to lodge a separate declaration of authorisation in Form CM1. A patent can be renewed 3 months before the renewal due date. If a patent is not renewed by the renewal due date, it may be renewed within 6 months with additional late payment fees (status updated to 'Lapsed (late renewal possible)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renew early (within 3-month pre-renewal window) to avoid late fees; third parties or non-agents may renew but ensure correct payment and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: First renewal timing if grant delayed beyond 45 months
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent was granted after 45 months from date of filing, the first renewal will only be payable within 3 months from the date of grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that long examination timelines alter the timing of the first renewal due date; follow given examples to compute correct due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: System checks on renewal requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the renewal request is received, the system will perform checks – a. Renewal fee has been paid; b. The application has proceeded to grant; c. The patent status is in force or lapsed (late renewal possible); d. The form is filed within 3 months before the renewal due date or within 6 months after the renewal due date; e. Renewal fee and any additional fee are correct (halved for LOR); f. The patent has not been renewed for the same year; g. If renewal is for 21st year or above, patent term extension has been approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If checks pass, the patent will be automatically renewed by the system and entry made in the register/Patents Journal. If checks fail, Formalities officer will invite clarification/rectification within 2 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification and refusal outcomes for renewal requests
rubrics_metrics.description: To rectify errors, applicant may file Form CM4 (select 'Correction of Form lodged' for errors on the form). If the patent is not due for renewal or has already been renewed, the Formalities officer will refuse the renewal and initiate a refund request. If the patent has lapsed due to non-payment, the Formalities officer will refuse the renewal and invite the applicant to request restoration by filing Patents Form 19 together with a Statutory Declaration. If there is insufficient payment due to miscalculation of the renewal fees payable, the Formalities officer will refuse the application and invite the applicant to put in a new request with the correct fees; a refund job will be initiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CM4 to correct payment or form errors. Restoration requires Form 19 and statutory declaration; anticipate refunds for refused/incorrect renewals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal reminders and limits of reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The system will automatically issue a notification to renewal agent on record or the last person who renewed the patent to inform that the window for renewal is open. This is not intended to be a replacement of the proprietor's tracking system, but rather as an additional service. The absence of this letter is not a valid reason for the proprietor to miss the renewal and extension will not be allowed for the payment of renewal fee with no additional fees after the prescribed period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on IPOS reminders; maintain independent renewal tracking to avoid lapsing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overdue renewals, second reminders and temporary extension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the renewal payment is overdue, the system will automatically issue a second notification to the renewal agent/last person who renewed to inform that the payment is overdue and invite renewal with late fees. The status will be updated to 'Lapsed (late renewal possible)'. If the second reminder was not issued within 1 month from the renewal due date, the Registry will extend the timeline to allow payment of the renewal fees within 2 months with no additional fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for status changes and act on second reminders. The Registry may grant a short extension only in specific reminder-failure cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lapse, restoration windows and permanent lapse
rubrics_metrics.description: The system will update the status of the patent to 'Lapsed (restoration possible)' at the end of 6 months following the renewal date and a notification will be sent inviting restoration. At the end of 18 months (for renewal due on or after 14 Feb 14) from the renewal due date, if the patent has not been restored and no restoration request is pending, the patent status will be updated to 'Lapsed' (permanent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration must be requested within the prescribed restoration window; after permanent lapse, restoration is not available under normal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent expiry and register update practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the patent term is up (20 years from filing or end of extended term), the system will update the status of the patent to 'Expired' and make an entry on the register and in the Patents Journal. The expiry is effective as of the original expiry date, though register updates may be withheld if restoration, patent term extension or surrender requests are pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expiry is effective from the legal expiry date; administrative status updates follow once pending matters are resolved. Patent term extension rules affect expiry dates.
